sources.entry: instructor - A library for extracting structured data from LLMs, powered by Pydantic.

summary.one_liner: Instructor is a Python library that gets structured, Pydantic-validated data out of LLM responses across many providers.
summary.what_it_does: Lets you define a Pydantic model and pass it as response_model to an LLM client, returning a typed, validated object instead of raw text or JSON. The README shows a client created with instructor.from_provider("provider/model") and a single chat.completions.create call that returns a User instance. It describes automatic retries when Pydantic validation fails, with the validation error fed back to the model. Examples cover OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama, and Groq, including passing API keys directly instead of environment variables. The README also points to PydanticAI for users who need full agent runs, typed tools, and evals.
use_cases: extract structured fields from free text
get reliable JSON from an LLM
validate LLM output with Pydantic models
switch between LLM providers with one API
automatic retries on malformed model output
structured data extraction from natural language
notable: Single interface for many LLM providers via instructor.from_provider
Failed Pydantic validations are retried with the error message
Uses plain Pydantic models as the schema definition
Companion to PydanticAI for agent workflows
caveats: The README excerpt does not state a license
Richer agent features are pointed to PydanticAI rather than provided here
Provider support depends on each provider's API and the model names given in examples
